subject: Game Theory
title: Quadratic Voting
description: A fast breakdown of Quadratic Voting for builders.

hook.text: You care deeply about education but not about traffic policy. Standard voting gives you one vote on each. That's wrong.

buildup.text: Quadratic voting lets you buy extra votes, but costs rise quadratically: 1 vote costs 1, 2 cost 4, 3 cost 9.

discovery.text: Glen Weyl showed this optimally balances intensity and equality: passionate voters invest more, but at rising cost.

twist.text: Colorado used quadratic voting in its legislature. Lawmakers allocated budgets across bills based on real priorities.

climax.text: Crypto governance adopted it: Gitcoin uses quadratic funding to allocate millions to public goods projects.

punchline.text: Vote harder on what matters most to you.

quiz.question: How does quadratic voting measure preference intensity?
